title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Entitlement Restoration Terms by Program
content:
Three program terms of the VA Home Loan Guaranty govern how entitlement charged to a loan can come back to the veteran: whether an assuming veteran may substitute their entitlement so that the seller's is restored; whether a veteran who paid the loan in full but still owns the property may restore entitlement once; and whether ordinary restoration requires the property to have been sold or otherwise disposed of.

## Terms by program

| Program | Assuming veteran may substitute entitlement | One-time restoration while still owning the property | Ordinary restoration requires the property to be sold or otherwise disposed of |
|---|---|---|---|
| VA Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| VA Manufactured Home Loan | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| VA Purchase Loan (10% or More Down) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| VA Purchase Loan (5% to Less Than 10% Down) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| VA Purchase Loan (Less Than 5% Down) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| VA Cash-Out Refinance Loan | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Native American Direct Loan (NADL) | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## Questions the terms answer

**Is substitution of entitlement available on every program?** Yes; all seven programs allow it.

**Does a veteran who has paid the loan in full but kept the home have any route to restoration under the program terms?** Yes; every program allows the one-time restoration for a veteran who paid the loan in full but still owns the property.

**Is disposal of the property part of ordinary restoration?** Yes, on every program.
